protections: P1: OIDC email-fallback linking to an existing local account must only trust an email the provider asserts as verified (email_verified), taken from the same claim source as the email itself.

P2: OIDC email-fallback linking must only bind to a local account whose own email ownership has been established (not a local account still in email-confirmation-required state); the OIDC callback has no equivalent of the password-login confirmation gate.

evidence: pkg/modules/auth/openid/openid.go:75-83 (claims struct has no email_verified field)
pkg/modules/auth/openid/openid.go:361-391 (fallback search keyed on Issuer=local plus cl.Email, no verification check)
pkg/modules/auth/openid/openid.go:374-376 (comment acknowledges providers that set email without verification)
config-raw.json:775 (docs warn emailfallback can allow account hijacking)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: A check reading email_verified from the ID token looks complete; the merge only fills blanks or honours an admin-set forceuserinfo flag.
evidence: pkg/modules/auth/openid/openid.go:440 (email replaced by userinfo email when forceUserInfo or token email empty; any verified flag must travel with it)
pkg/modules/auth/openid/openid.go:484 (userinfo is fetched whenever any of email/name/username/picture is missing, so mixed-source claims are the common path)
pkg/modules/auth/openid/openid.go:498 (merge result feeds getOrCreateUser fallback at :377)
pkg/modules/auth/openid/openid.go:478-482 (a strictly typed email_verified field that fails to decode, e.g. string "true", aborts the whole login)
pkg/modules/auth/openid/openid.go:393-409 (new-user creation from OIDC must keep working when email_verified is absent/false)
pkg/modules/auth/openid/openid.go:353,410 (already-linked issuer+subject logins must keep working regardless of email_verified)
pkg/modules/auth/openid/openid_test.go:257-275 (fallback-on-email fixture uses claims with no email_verified; whether that must keep passing is a design choice)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about the provider's claim; the local account row is first-party data and the account is not disabled or locked.
evidence: pkg/user/user.go:324-330 (getUser only errors on disabled/locked, so fallback matches a local account in email-confirmation-required state)
pkg/user/user.go:370-373 (password login refuses StatusEmailConfirmationRequired; OIDC path has no counterpart)
pkg/user/user_create.go:96-100 (local signups are unconfirmed until the mail link is used when a mailer is configured)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Writing the claim email onto the caller's own already-linked account does not link to any other account.
evidence: pkg/modules/auth/openid/openid.go:413-415 (unverified claim email persisted on every login)
pkg/user/user.go:576-586 (uniqueness check is scoped to issuer+subject, so it can duplicate a local user's email)
pkg/user/user_password_reset.go:110 (reset lookup by bare email returns the first matching row)

masking: A's TOTP gate (pkg/modules/auth/openid/openid.go:212-220, helper :126-153) runs after getOrCreateUser, so B's fallback takeover is blocked only for victims with TOTP enabled; B stays fully open for victims without TOTP. A does not unmask B; B's hidden tests need a non-TOTP victim.

conflicts.what: The natural T1 fix (require email_verified==true) applied to the whole callback or the claims decode breaks new-user creation and existing linked logins for providers that omit email_verified or send it as a string; the check must gate only the fallback branch and decode leniently.

If the verified flag is merged independently of email (e.g. 'fill if blank'), a token-side email_verified=true can certify a userinfo-side email; the flag must follow whichever source supplied the email.

fairness_risks: Providers that never emit email_verified (or emit it only from userinfo) lose email fallback entirely; admins who knowingly enabled emailfallback (config-raw.json:775) for a trusted IdP may expect it to keep working. Hidden tests must not require fallback to work without the claim, and must not forbid an admin opt-in either.
email_verified sent as string "true" is a legitimate shape from some IdPs; a test that only accepts JSON bool would penalise a lenient decoder, and a strict bool field breaks login at openid.go:478.

Existing unit test pkg/modules/auth/openid/openid_test.go:257-275 expects fallback with no email_verified claim to link; the task must update or replace it, otherwise it conflicts with the security rule.

T4: refusing fallback to an unconfirmed local account is defensible, but some deployments run without a mailer (pkg/user/user_create.go:96), where local accounts are Active and never confirmed; a rule demanding 'confirmed' email cannot be expressed there.

design.why: T1 is the advisory route (easy anchor). T2 is an M5 merge trap: the verified flag must follow the email's source through mergeClaims, which a fallback-site-only check misses. T3 is the mimo-type coupled value: the gate must not break creation or linked logins and must tolerate absent or string email_verified. T4 is the deepseek-type absent protection with a strong reason to dismiss: fallback binds to an unconfirmed local account, and the OIDC callback lacks the confirmation gate that password login has. All four need separate fix judgements at different sites. T5 is left out because its impact is unproven.

unverified: B's published fix (7854f2729ab7) was not inspected; whether it also handles T2/T3/T4 is unknown.

T4 exploit impact: with a mailer configured, an attacker-created unconfirmed local account cannot be logged into by the attacker (user.go:371, user_password_reset.go:73), so the practical harm (victim data captured in an attacker-owned account later confirmable) is unconfirmed; without a mailer the state never occurs.
T5 impact: no path was found by which a duplicated unverified email on an OIDC user leads to takeover; included only as a candidate.
Which real IdPs send email_verified as a string, or only via userinfo, was not checked in this repo.

Username fallback (openid.go:368-372) matches the IdP subject to a local username without verification; it is documented as dangerous (config-raw.json:770) and is not recorded as a trap for this advisory.
